chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Aslam, who said:

When Abu Ja'far, meaning the son of Al-Reza (peace be upon him), wanted to shorten his hair for the Umrah, the barber wanted to take from the sides of the head, so he said to him: 'Begin with the forelocks', so he began with it.

key_terms.النَّاصِيَةِ: The forelocks / front of the head

ai.seo_question: How did the Imams trim their hair for Umrah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the specific Sunnah of starting the hair-cutting process for Umrah from the forelocks (an-nasiyah), a practice rooted in the Prophet’s tradition and affirmed by the Imams. It underscores the meticulous attention to ritual detail (adab) in Shia fiqh, distinguishing the recommended method from mere permissibility. The narration serves as a practical guide for pilgrims, linking physical grooming to spiritual intentionality during the state of Ihram.
